checks.finding:
**1. Two hunks tag depth on errors that already carry it, so they now hold it twice.**
`crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:331` and `crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:344` add `.with_depth(depth)` inside a closure whose next line (`:332`, `:345`) already wraps the result in `Error::WithDepth { depth, err: Box::new(err) }`. When `ent.file_type()` fails at depth 3, `from_entry` now returns `WithDepth{3, WithPath{p, WithDepth{3, Io}}}`. Before the PR it returned `WithDepth{3, WithPath{p, Io}}`, and `Error::depth()` (`lib.rs:252`) already gave `Some(3)`. So these hunks change nothing `depth()` can see. What they do change is the nesting of a public enum: a caller that matches `WithDepth { err, .. }`, then `WithPath { err, .. }`, then expects `Io` now hits a second `WithDepth`. c10f151's own message flags that kind of structural change as a possible break. Fix: revert both hunks. The `io::Error::from(err)` removals on those lines are identity conversions and can go back too.
checks.evidence: Read, not run (offline, read-only). On HEAD, crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:331 (from_entry) and :344 (cfg(windows) from_entry_os) are `let err = Error::Io(err).with_depth(depth).with_path(ent.path());` followed at :332/:345 by `Error::WithDepth { depth, err: Box::new(err) }`; git blame puts :331/:344 on the PR commit dafdd832 and :332/:345 on base (^a5ba50c). lib.rs:269-271 defines with_depth as `Error::WithDepth { depth, err: Box::new(self) }` and with_path as WithPath wrapping self, so the result is WithDepth{d, WithPath{p, WithDepth{d, Io}}} where base built WithDepth{d, WithPath{p, Io}}. lib.rs:252-257 depth() returns Some(depth) at the outer WithDepth, identical before and after; Display (lib.rs:339) and io_error/is_io/into_io_error (lib.rs:176, 216, 241) recurse through WithDepth, so the only change is the extra nesting a caller sees when matching the public enum. c10f151 (an ancestor of base) says in its message 'this could conceivably be a breaking change if callers were previously relying on down-casting nested errors'. The removed io::Error::from(err) calls are identity: ent.file_type()/ent.metadata() return io::Result, so err is already io::Error.

checks.finding:
**2. The Unix `metadata_internal` got depth; its Windows twin didn't.**
The diff changes the `#[cfg(not(windows))]` `DirEntryRaw::metadata_internal` (`walk.rs:304-306`) but leaves the `#[cfg(windows)]` one at `walk.rs:294` as `Error::Io(io::Error::from(err)).with_path(&self.path)`. Concrete case: on Windows, `DirEntry::metadata()` on a followed symlink whose target is gone returns an error with `depth() == None`; on Unix the same walk returns `Some(depth)`. Everywhere else the diff edits both cfg twins (`from_path` at `:394` and `:413`), so this one reads as missed. The same class has one more instance with depth in scope: `is_same_file_system` (`walk.rs:2024`), called from `walk.rs:1665` with `work.dent` right there, still returns `Error::Io(err).with_path(path)` with no depth. Either add depth at both or say in the body why they stay out.
checks.evidence: Read on HEAD, not run (needs a Windows target). The diff changes the #[cfg(not(windows))] DirEntryRaw::metadata_internal to `Error::Io(err).with_depth(self.depth).with_path(&self.path)` (crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:304-306), but the #[cfg(windows)] twin at walk.rs:287-295 still ends `.map_err(|err| Error::Io(io::Error::from(err)).with_path(&self.path))` (walk.rs:294). Its only fallible branch is `if self.follow_link { fs::metadata(&self.path) }`, so a followed symlink with a missing target errors there. DirEntryInner::metadata passes Raw errors through unwrapped (`Raw(ref x) => x.metadata()`, walk.rs:186), and Error::depth (crates/ignore/src/lib.rs:252-258) returns Some only via a WithDepth layer, so on Windows depth() is None while Unix gets Some(depth). The diff does edit both twins elsewhere: windows from_path (walk.rs:393-394), unix from_path (walk.rs:412-413), and even the windows-only from_entry_os (walk.rs:343-344), so the windows metadata_internal reads as missed. git blame shows walk.rs:288-295 unchanged since base (^a5ba50c); the gap is a platform divergence the PR's own edit creates. The secondary note also holds: is_same_file_system (walk.rs:2022-2025) still does `Error::Io(err).with_path(path)` with no depth, called at walk.rs:1665 with work.dent in scope; that line is pre-existing (^a5ba50c) and untouched by the diff, so it is an omission against the PR's stated goal rather than a regression.
